svg.title: Figure 3. Unequal potential butterfly host opportunities across introduced plants and documented butterflies
svg.desc: Cumulative contributions of 670 introduced known-host plant species, original 239-butterfly native resource geographic breadth versus added island food opportunities, and gains among butterflies recorded from one host-plant family. All values are from frozen documented HOSTS and WCVP and do not indicate population changes.
svg.text: 3 | Unequal resource redistribution across plants and butterflies
Source-defined potential larval food geography — fixed known host identities, no new observed butterfly establishment
670 accepted contributing plants; 38 supply half the added units
Top k documented host plants (log scale)
Share of all added butterfly–region units (%)
Prior host geography predicts absolute island gains
239 butterflies; native resource regions vs added island regions
Gains reach butterflies documented from a single host-plant family
Fraction of butterfly species gaining ≥1 known-host region (not a host-quality measure)
Top-k curve connects verified selected k summaries; scatter plots all 239 source butterflies. Opportunity, not actual feeding or demographic benefit.
